what_this_is: The RAPTOR measurement re-taken after Phase 16a, which is the act that phase exists to make meaningful (`12-roadmap.md` §3). Three arms on the ten fetch-tier PDFs, each run given its own fresh store, persisted as `weft eval run` records and held to this statement by `tests/docs/test_raptor_baseline.py`.
why_it_is_not_a_replay: The 2026-09-07 exit's own question file lived in a scratch directory and was thrown away, so its subject could not be reconstructed — the defect 16.5 and 16.6 were built to end. This set is *derived*: `eval/raptor-baseline/build_questions.py` selects it through `check_questions.reproducible_questions` over the fetch tier, narrowed to PDF-labelled questions, with labels as the manifest's own corpus-relative paths. 83 questions, of which 66 are scoreable for mean_average_precision — which is where the exit's own `n=66` came from, so the two measurements are over the same questions after all, and now provably so: every record carries the question-set digest.
each_arm_replaces: the `extract` stage with `pdf-text` and the `embed` stage with `openai-embeddings`, and nothing else — so what is measured is the shipped rung, thresholds included, against a real embedder. The three documents are committed at `eval/raptor-baseline/pipelines/`, which the 2026-09-07 exit's were not.
repetitions_are: Six for each raptor arm and three for the leaves arm, as the exit's own statement set.
each_run_has_its_own_store: Every run truncates `weft_nodes`, `weft_sources` and `weft_node_productions`, asserts the store empty before and non-empty after, and nothing else touches the container while it runs (`L8.30`). Throwaway database `weft_raptor16`, dropped afterwards.
summariser: openai:gpt-5.4-mini, via `[llm.roles] index` — recorded on every record as `role:index`, which the 2026-09-07 records could not hold.
what_it_says: A null result for one-level RAPTOR and a small, reliable *regression* for the multi-level one. Against leaves, one-level's paired interval straddles zero on four of five metrics; multi-level's is entirely below zero on mean_average_precision (-0.023, 95% CI -0.047 to -0.005), mrr@3 and ndcg@3. One-level and multi-level are indistinguishable from each other on every metric. Phase 10 reported a null result and this sharpens it: the deeper variant is not merely no better, it is slightly worse.
why_the_two_intervals_disagree: The between-run verdict reports `outside-baseline-spread` on every metric, and it is an artefact: the leaves arm is deterministic, so its three repetitions span zero width and *any* difference falls outside it — which the verdict line says out loud. The paired interval over questions (task 16.9) is the one that answers whether a difference generalises, and it disagrees on four of five metrics. This is the case that task existed for, and it is the reason both are printed rather than one.
twelve_questions_the_exit_scored_and_thi: `precision@3`, `recall@3`, `ndcg@3` and `mrr@3` report n=54 with 12 excluded, where the 2026-09-07 records report n=66. Task 16.7 is why: a metric named @k that retrieved fewer than k candidates now refuses rather than reporting a number over what it has. So twelve of the exit's own per-question scores were claims its retrieval could not support.
facts_not_recorded_is: Empty, and it is the first statement in this tree for which that is true. Every fact `weft eval compare` compares — the corpus digest's basis, the query rung, the distribution versions, the question-set identity and the per-question scores — is carried by all fifteen records. See `tests/docs/test_raptor_baseline.py`, ledger 16.2.
